title: FluencyCraft Intermediate - Day 13

questions.question: Day 13 Practice (Technical Demos & Walkthroughs (Phase 2)): When talking about rescheduling a team sync (twice a week), which sentence is grammatically correct for 'Our neighbor'?

options.a: I am rescheduling a team sync right now.
options.b: Could we reschedule our sync meeting to 3:00 PM?
options.c: Shift meeting 3 clock possible? yesterday
options.d: Shift meeting 3 clock possible?

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option B
Natural everyday English uses standard tense agreement: "Could we reschedule our sync meeting to 3:00 PM?".

questions.question: Day 13 Practice (Technical Demos & Walkthroughs (Phase 2)): When talking about checking grocery item stock (yesterday afternoon), which sentence is grammatically correct for 'My manager'?

options.a: Milk packet no stock having. yesterday
options.b: I am checking grocery item stock right now.
options.c: Milk packet no stock having.
options.d: Fresh milk packets were completely out of stock.

questions.explanation:

Natural everyday English uses standard tense agreement: "Fresh milk packets were completely out of stock.".

questions.question: Day 13 Vocabulary (Technical Demos & Walkthroughs (Phase 2)): What is the exact practical meaning of the phrase 'follow up'?

options.a: To clean or inspect a physical room thoroughly.
options.b: Check progress on a prior matter.
options.c: To postpone or cancel an activity indefinitely.
options.d: To perform a daily task hastily without preparation.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option B
'follow up' means: check progress on a prior matter. Example: "I will follow up with the team regarding the report."

questions.question: Day 13 Vocabulary (Technical Demos & Walkthroughs (Phase 2)): What is the exact practical meaning of the phrase 'drop off'?

options.a: To clean or inspect a physical room thoroughly.
options.b: To postpone or cancel an activity indefinitely.
options.c: Take someone to a destination and leave them there.
options.d: To perform a daily task hastily without preparation.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option C
'drop off' means: take someone to a destination and leave them there. Example: "Please drop me off near the bus stand."

questions.question: Day 13 Vocabulary (Technical Demos & Walkthroughs (Phase 2)): What is the exact practical meaning of the phrase 'drop by'?

options.b: To perform a daily task hastily without preparation.

questions.explanation:

'drop by' means: visit someone informally for a short time. Example: "Feel free to drop by our home this evening."

questions.question: Day 13 Vocabulary (Technical Demos & Walkthroughs (Phase 2)): What is the exact practical meaning of the phrase 'order in'?

questions.question:
Day 13 Translation Scenario 1 (Technical Demos & Walkthroughs (Phase 2)):

Telugu: "నాకు కొంచెం తలనొప్పిగా ఉంది, ఒక గంట సేపు రెస్ట్ తీసుకుంటాను."
(Literal attempt: "To me little headache is there, take rest one hour.")

options.a: I am needing to to me little headache is there, take rest one hour.
options.b: Literal Indian English phrasing without modal polite verbs.
options.c: To me little headache is there, take rest one hour.
options.d: I have a slight headache; I'm going to rest for an hour.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option D
Natural Version: "I have a slight headache; I'm going to rest for an hour."

Say 'I have a slight headache' instead of literal translations.

questions.question:
Day 13 Translation Scenario 2 (Technical Demos & Walkthroughs (Phase 2)):

Telugu: "నేను సాధారణంగా ఉదయం 6 గంటలకే నిద్రలేచి ఒక కప్పు టీ తాగుతాను."
(Literal attempt: "I generally in morning 6 clock wake up drink tea.")

options.a: I usually wake up at 6:00 AM and have a cup of tea.
options.b: Literal Indian English phrasing without modal polite verbs.
options.c: I am needing to i generally in morning 6 clock wake up drink tea.
options.d: I generally in morning 6 clock wake up drink tea.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option A
Natural Version: "I usually wake up at 6:00 AM and have a cup of tea."

Use 'have a cup of tea' and specify time as '6:00 AM'.

questions.question:
Day 13 Translation Scenario 3 (Technical Demos & Walkthroughs (Phase 2)):

Telugu: "ముందుగా సమస్య యొక్క మూలకారణాన్ని కనుగొనాలి."
(Literal attempt: "First problem root cause finding wanted.")

options.a: First problem root cause finding wanted.
options.b: I am needing to first problem root cause finding wanted.
options.c: Literal Indian English phrasing without modal polite verbs.
options.d: First and foremost, we must identify the root cause of the issue.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option D
Natural Version: "First and foremost, we must identify the root cause of the issue."

Use 'First and foremost' and 'identify the root cause'.

questions.question:

(Literal attempt: "My parcel today evening delivery becoming?")

options.a: My parcel today evening delivery becoming?
options.b: I am needing to my parcel today evening delivery becoming?
options.c: Literal Indian English phrasing without modal polite verbs.
options.d: Will my package be delivered by this evening?

questions.explanation:

Use 'Will my package be delivered...' for delivery tracking.
